added_lemmas.statement:
Put \(a=1-\alpha\), \(p_s=2+1/s\),
\(C_b=2(4H_s/M)^{1/s}\), and \(B_n=\sqrt{C_bT_n}\).  For every
\(n\ge1\) and \(0<\kappa_n\le1/8\),
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)
 =\begin{cases}
 2a-\dfrac{4s}{4s+1}B_n,&B_n\le a,\\[6pt]
 \dfrac{2a(2s+1)}{4s+1}
 \left(\dfrac{a}{B_n}\right)^{2s/(2s+1)},&B_n>a.
 \end{cases}
\]
If in addition \(\kappa_n\le1/16\), then
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)
 \ge\max\{G_\alpha(\tau_n),F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\},
\]
where
\[
 G_\alpha(\tau_n)=
 \begin{cases}
 2a-\dfrac{16}{3}\sqrt{\tau_n},
 &0\le\tau_n\le a^2/16,\\[6pt]
 \dfrac{a^3}{24\tau_n},&\tau_n>a^2/16.
 \end{cases}
\]
Moreover, there are constants \(c_{\mathrm{fix}}>0\) and
\(C_{\mathrm{low}}>0\), depending only on \(s\), \(M\), and
\(\alpha\), such that for every \(n\ge1\) and
\(0<\kappa_n\le1/8\),
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)
 \ge c_{\mathrm{fix}}\min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}\right\},
 \qquad
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge C_{\mathrm{low}}r_n.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\ge1\), \(s\in[1,2]\), \(M\ge2\),
\(0<\kappa_n\le1/8\), and a measurable connected-interval rule
\(I_n\) satisfying the honesty constraint in
\(\text{def:minimax-length}\).  Write
\[
 a=1-\alpha>0,\qquad
 p_s=2+\frac1s,\qquad
 C_b=2\left(\frac{4H_s}{M}\right)^{1/s}>0,
 \qquad T_n=n\kappa_n^{p_s},
\]
and set \(B_n=\sqrt{C_bT_n}\).  All probabilities below are for the
observed sample \((O_1,\ldots,O_n)\).

We first integrate the fixed-cutoff continuum.  By
\(\text{prop:fixed-cutoff-bump-membership-kl}\), for every
\(u\in[-1,1]\), both \(Q_u\) and \(Q_0\) belong to \(\mathcal P_n\),
their effect labels are \(u\) and \(0\), respectively, and
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_u^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le
 \{C_bn(\kappa_n|u|)^{p_s}\}^{1/2}
 =B_n|u|^{p_s/2}.
 \tag{1}
\]
The last equality uses \(T_n=n\kappa_n^{p_s}\).  For the measurable
event \(A_u=\{u\in I_n\}\), the definition
\(\operatorname{TV}(Q_u^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
=\sup_A|Q_u^{\otimes n}(A)-Q_0^{\otimes n}(A)|\) and honesty under
\(Q_u\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_0^{\otimes n}(A_u)
 &\ge Q_u^{\otimes n}(A_u)
       -\operatorname{TV}(Q_u^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})\\
 &\ge a-B_n|u|^{p_s/2}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Since a probability is nonnegative,
\[
 Q_0^{\otimes n}\{u\in I_n\}
 \ge\bigl[a-B_n|u|^{p_s/2}\bigr]_+.
 \tag{2}
\]

For completeness, we pass from the pointwise bounds to expected length
without assuming an unmentioned continuum measurability theorem.  For
\(m\ge1\), let \(u_{j,m}=-1+2j/m\), \(j=0,\ldots,m\).  Every connected
subset \(J\) of \([-1,1]\) is an interval, and points of this grid are
spaced by \(2/m\).  Therefore
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^m\mathbf 1\{u_{j,m}\in J\}
 \le1+\frac m2|J|,
\]
including the empty and singleton cases.  With \(J=I_n\), rearrangement,
finite-sum linearity, and (2) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_{Q_0}|I_n|
 &\ge \frac2m\sum_{j=0}^m
 Q_0^{\otimes n}\{u_{j,m}\in I_n\}-\frac2m\\
 &\ge \frac2m\sum_{j=0}^m
 \bigl[a-B_n|u_{j,m}|^{p_s/2}\bigr]_+-\frac2m.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{3}
\]
The summand is a continuous function of \(u\in[-1,1]\).  Hence the
equally spaced Riemann sums in (3) converge as \(m\to\infty\), and
symmetry gives
\[
 E_{Q_0}|I_n|
 \ge \int_{-1}^1\bigl[a-B_n|u|^{p_s/2}\bigr]_+\,du
 =2\int_0^1\bigl[a-B_nt^{p_s/2}\bigr]_+\,dt
 =F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n).
 \tag{4}
\]
Because \(Q_0\in\mathcal P_n\), (4) is a lower bound for the worst-case
expected length of this arbitrary honest rule.  Taking the infimum over
such rules in \(\text{def:minimax-length}\) proves
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)
 \qquad(0<\kappa_n\le1/8).
 \tag{5}
\]

We now evaluate the integral in (4).  Put
\(\beta=p_s/2=(2s+1)/(2s)\).  If \(B_n\le a\), the integrand is
nonnegative on \([0,1]\), so
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)
 &=2\left(a-\frac{B_n}{\beta+1}\right)\\
 &=2a-\frac{4s}{4s+1}B_n.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{6}
\]
If \(B_n>a\), the positive region is
\(0\le t\le t_0\), where
\[
 t_0=\left(\frac a{B_n}\right)^{1/\beta}
 =\left(\frac a{B_n}\right)^{2s/(2s+1)}<1.
\]
Using \(B_nt_0^\beta=a\), direct integration gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)
 &=2\left(at_0-\frac{B_nt_0^{\beta+1}}{\beta+1}\right)\\
 &=2at_0\frac{\beta}{\beta+1}\\
 &=\frac{2a(2s+1)}{4s+1}
 \left(\frac a{B_n}\right)^{2s/(2s+1)}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{7}
\]
Equations (6)--(7) prove the asserted two-piece formula, including the
common boundary value when \(B_n=a\).

Suppose next that \(\kappa_n\le1/16\).  By
\(\text{prop:moving-cutoff-membership-kl}\), for every
\(t\in[-1,1]\), \(P_t,P_0\in\mathcal P_n\),
\(\theta_{P_t}=t\), and
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(P_t^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \le4\sqrt{\tau_n|t|}.
 \tag{8}
\]
Repeating the event comparison and the finite-grid argument in
(2)--(4), now with (8), yields
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)
 \ge2\int_0^1[a-4\sqrt{\tau_nt}]_+\,dt
 =G_\alpha(\tau_n).
 \tag{9}
\]
To verify the displayed closed form, if
\(\tau_n\le a^2/16\), the integrand in (9) is nonnegative throughout
\([0,1]\), and
\[
 2\int_0^1(a-4\sqrt{\tau_nt})\,dt
 =2a-\frac{16}{3}\sqrt{\tau_n}.
 \tag{10}
\]
If \(\tau_n>a^2/16\), its positive region ends at
\(t_1=a^2/(16\tau_n)\), and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 2\int_0^{t_1}(a-4\sqrt{\tau_nt})\,dt
 &=2\left(at_1-\frac83\sqrt{\tau_n}t_1^{3/2}\right)\\
 &=\frac{a^3}{24\tau_n}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{11}
\]
Combining (5) and (9) proves
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)
 \ge\max\{G_\alpha(\tau_n),F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\}
 \qquad(\kappa_n\le1/16).
 \tag{12}
\]

It remains to derive the stated coarse frontier uniformly over the
whole strength shell.  Define
\[
 A_n=\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}>0.
\]
Because \(p_s=(2s+1)/s\) and
\(\rho_n=n^{-s/(2s+1)}\),
\[
 n\rho_n^{p_s}=1,
 \qquad
 T_n=n\kappa_n^{p_s}=A_n^{-p_s},
 \qquad
 B_n=\sqrt{C_b}\,A_n^{-p_s/2}.
 \tag{13}
\]
Let
\[
 \gamma=\min\left\{1,
 \left(\frac{a}{2\sqrt{C_b}}\right)^{2/p_s}\right\}>0.
\]
For \(0\le t\le\gamma\min\{1,A_n\}\), one has
\(t/A_n\le\gamma\): if \(A_n\le1\), this follows from
\(t\le\gamma A_n\), and if \(A_n\ge1\), it follows from
\(t\le\gamma\le\gamma A_n\).  Thus (13) and the definition of
\(\gamma\) imply
\[
 B_nt^{p_s/2}
 =\sqrt{C_b}\left(\frac t{A_n}\right)^{p_s/2}
 \le\sqrt{C_b}\gamma^{p_s/2}
 \le\frac a2.
\]
Restricting the integral in (4) to this interval gives
\[
 F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)
 \ge a\gamma\min\{1,A_n\}.
 \tag{14}
\]
Consequently (5) proves the fixed-cutoff bound with
\(c_{\mathrm{fix}}=a\gamma>0\), which depends only on
\(\alpha,s,M\) because \(H_s\) is fixed by \(s\) in
\(\text{def:fixed-cutoff-bump-continuum}\).

The formula (10)--(11) also implies, for every \(\tau>0\),
\[
 G_\alpha(\tau)
 \ge c_g\min\{1,\tau^{-1}\},
 \qquad c_g=\frac{a^3}{24}>0.
 \tag{15}
\]
Indeed, on \(0<\tau\le a^2/16\), (10) is at least \(2a/3\),
which is at least \(a^3/24\) because \(0<a<1\).  On
\(a^2/16<\tau\le1\), (11) is at least \(a^3/24\), and on
\(\tau>1\), (11) equals \(a^3/(24\tau)\).

Let
\[
 D_n=\frac1{n\kappa_n^3}=\tau_n^{-1}.
\]
If \(\kappa_n\le1/16\), (12), (14), and (15) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)
 &\ge\max\{c_{\mathrm{fix}}\min(1,A_n),
                    c_g\min(1,D_n)\}\\
 &\ge\frac12\min\{c_{\mathrm{fix}},c_g\}
       \{\min(1,A_n)+\min(1,D_n)\}\\
 &\ge\frac12\min\{c_{\mathrm{fix}},c_g\}
       \min\{1,A_n+D_n\}\\
 &=\frac12\min\{c_{\mathrm{fix}},c_g\}\,r_n.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{16}
\]
The penultimate inequality follows by cases: if \(A_n+D_n\le1\),
both terms on the preceding line equal \(A_n,D_n\); otherwise their
sum is at least one.

Finally suppose \(1/16<\kappa_n\le1/8\).  Positivity permits division,
and the definitions of \(A_n,D_n,\rho_n\) give
\[
 \frac{D_n}{A_n}
 =\frac1{n\kappa_n^2\rho_n}
 \le256\,n^{-(s+1)/(2s+1)}
 \le256,
 \tag{17}
\]
where \(\kappa_n>1/16\) gives \(\kappa_n^{-2}<256\), while
\(n\rho_n=n^{(s+1)/(2s+1)}\ge1\) because \(n\ge1\) and
\(s\in[1,2]\).  Hence
\[
 r_n=\min\{1,A_n+D_n\}
 \le257\min\{1,A_n\}.
 \tag{18}
\]
Combining (14), (5), and (18) yields
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge\frac{c_{\mathrm{fix}}}{257}r_n.
 \tag{19}
\]
Thus the choice
\[
 C_{\mathrm{low}}
 =\min\left\{\frac12\min(c_{\mathrm{fix}},c_g),
                    \frac{c_{\mathrm{fix}}}{257}\right\}>0
\]
works for every \(n\ge1\) and every \(0<\kappa_n\le1/8\), completing
the proof.
added_lemmas.justification: The two legal causal continua can both be integrated over their effect labels, giving explicit location--slope and fixed-cutoff lower envelopes and the complete lower half of the candidate all-strength frontier.
added_lemmas.gap: Known-cutoff weak-fuzzy procedures do not supply the moving-location term, while sharp unknown-cutoff rates do not supply the weak causal-ratio term; this theorem derives both within one unchanged full model and retains their finite-information lower values.
added_lemmas.consumer: An analyst obtains a design-independent impossibility benchmark: every honest connected interval obeys the explicit fixed-cutoff envelope, the moving-cutoff envelope where that witness is legal, and consequently the global rate lower bound \(C_{\mathrm{low}}r_n\).

proposed.name: F_{\alpha,s,M}
proposed.construction:
For \(T\ge0\), put
\[
 p_s=2+\frac1s,\qquad
 C_b=2\left(\frac{4H_s}{M}\right)^{1/s},\qquad
 B(T)=\sqrt{C_bT},\qquad a=1-\alpha,
\]
and define
\[
 F_{\alpha,s,M}(T)
 =2\int_0^1\bigl[a-B(T)t^{p_s/2}\bigr]_+\,dt
 =\begin{cases}
 2a-\dfrac{4s}{4s+1}B(T),&B(T)\le a,\\[6pt]
 \dfrac{2a(2s+1)}{4s+1}
 \left\{\dfrac{a}{B(T)}\right\}^{2s/(2s+1)},&B(T)>a.
 \end{cases}
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: Integrating the established continuum total-variation inequality produces this exact two-piece envelope; naming it makes the strengthened converse computable.

The old theorem is strictly subsumed by the directed integrated fixed-cutoff result. Because claim changes may only narrow an existing node, the stronger proved theorem is installed under a fresh identifier and all inbound dependencies are migrated atomically.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}=\operatorname{hull}\{\vartheta\in\Theta:\inf_{c\in\mathcal G_c}\Delta_n(c,\vartheta)\le\Gamma_n(\delta_n)\}\). The proved converse is \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\) over the full declared strength shell and, when \(\kappa_n\le1/16\), \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge\max\{G_\alpha(\tau_n),F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\}\); in particular \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\) globally. The matching profile upper comparison \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\asymp r_n\) remains proposed only on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The headline functional must record the newly proved explicit fixed-cutoff envelope while preserving the distinction between the converse and the still-open profile upper bound.

proposed.comparator_claim: Their unknown-threshold result transfers the minimax rate for estimating a sharp-RD discontinuity location from a convolution white-noise model.
Their moderate-break analysis derives a Gaussian-process limit experiment and a nearly weighted-average-power maximizing test.
Their Theorem 1 gives uniformly asymptotically valid conditional tests with a functional nuisance parameter.
Their Theorem 1 shows that risk functions attainable in the weak-GMM Gaussian-process experiment bound finite-sample asymptotic risk.
Their Theorem 3.1 characterizes optimal one-sided confidence intervals through an ordered modulus over convex fixed-index regression classes.

prose_updates.tldr: For fuzzy regression discontinuity with a weak compliance jump and unknown cutoff, cutoff recovery and causal-effect informativeness are distinct. The moving-cutoff continuum gives the explicit finite-sample lower value \(G_\alpha(\tau_n)\), while integration of the entire causal-valid fixed-cutoff bump continuum gives the explicit two-piece value \(F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\). Their maximum proves the global converse \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\) under the unchanged binary separate-sided Holder class, and the existing upper bound gives the exact flat-face limit \(2(1-\alpha)\). Finite-grid four-cell calibration remains valid for every compatible treatment--outcome association, including singular cells. The open kernel is the \(s=1\) critical decision value and a continuum-honest, support-wide profile interval with controlled stochastic, discretization, certificate, and fallback remainders; no profile upper rate or finite-positive critical value is claimed as proved.

project_justification.gap: Known-cutoff weak-fuzzy inference, sharp-RD unknown-cutoff rates, generic weak-identification decision theory, and Bayesian propagation of cutoff uncertainty have been developed separately. None supplies explicit all-label lower decision values together with an attaining honest connected interval when the cutoff and fuzzy denominator weaken jointly; both causal-continuum lower envelopes are now proved here, whereas attainment remains open.
project_justification.niche: The preserved binary uniform-design class makes two complementary causal lifts explicit while leaving the observable treatment--outcome association unrestricted. A moving-cutoff continuum measures slope-location ambiguity, and a fixed-cutoff compact bump continuum now yields an integrated all-label value rather than only a two-point rate. The resulting nonregular location/effect problem is neither a fixed-boundary modulus problem nor a parametric unknown-break problem.
project_justification.fill: The project proves \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\) throughout the declared strength shell and \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge\max\{G_\alpha(\tau_n),F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\}\) on the legal moving-cutoff range, yielding \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\) globally. It also defines a support-wide four-cell profile and exact coarsened calibration that leave association free. The matching upper frontier, complete critical experiment, and total attaining interval remain unresolved.

prose_updates.related_work: Hahn, Todd, and van der Klaauw (2001) supply the local Wald identification argument. Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) and Noack and Rothe (2024, Theorem 1) give weak-identification-robust inference at a fixed known cutoff; the present known-cutoff result is an exact singleton-cutoff finite-grid calibration and reduction under unrestricted permitted treatment--outcome association, not a claim of first-order residual-jump equivalence. The fixed-cutoff bump continuum now yields the explicit integrated value \(F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\), while the moving-cutoff continuum adds the distinct \(1/(n\kappa_n^3)\) difficulty and its explicit integrated value \(G_\alpha\). Porter and Yu (2015, Sections 3--5) and Tuvaandorj (2020, Sections 3--4) study unknown-location behavior predominantly in sharp designs, without this weak causal ratio or connected honest-length criterion. Elliott and M{\"u}ller (2014, Sections 2.1--2.3) motivate process experiments for moderate unknown breaks, but do not solve the present Holder-margin decision problem. Andrews and Mikusheva (2016, Theorem 1) and Andrews and Mikusheva (2022, Theorem 1 and Section 4) inform nuisance calibration and weak-decision analysis; Armstrong and Koles{\'a}r (2018, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A.4) connect testing power to expected length over convex fixed-index classes. None proves the still-open support-wide profile upper bound over the translated nonconvex union. Arai, Hsu, Kitagawa, Mourifi{\'e}, and Wan (2022, Section 2) motivate retaining the full joint outcome--treatment law. Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas (2025 version, Sections 3 and 6) propagate unknown-cutoff uncertainty in a Bayesian model without uniform frequentist honesty or minimax length.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The model has no outcome-variance, null-residual-variance, covariance-eigenvalue, or joint-cell positivity floor, and the strengthened lower bound adds none. The proved results include the moving-cutoff causal lift and its Kullback--Leibler bound, the explicit integrated value \(G_\alpha(\tau_n)\), the fixed-cutoff compact-bump causal lift and its \(n(\kappa_n|u|)^{2+1/s}\) divergence bound, the new integrated fixed-cutoff value \(F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\), the exact flat-face limit, and the all-strength converse \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\). Exact singleton-cutoff finite-grid four-cell calibration and population false-split separation are also proved, uniformly over permitted binary treatment--outcome associations; the former is not a first-order residual-jump equivalence theorem. These facts do not establish continuum honesty, an upper expected-length rate, or attainment by \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}\). The finite-positive decision values, full-model least favorability, continuum discretization, localized stochastic profile bound, and negligible fallback risk remain open. A matching upper comparison is still only a proposed goal on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\). No smoothness of joint cells, conditional independence for the full class, association separation, cross-side derivative matching, oracle cutoff, or known association nuisance is imposed.

statement_notes.justification: The two legal causal continua are integrated label by label, yielding explicit decision lower values and the complete lower half of the candidate all-strength frontier.
statement_notes.gap: Known-cutoff weak-fuzzy procedures omit translated-cutoff ambiguity, while sharp unknown-cutoff rates omit the weak causal ratio; the theorem proves both lower mechanisms and their full-label envelopes inside one unchanged class.
statement_notes.consumer: An analyst can compare any honest connected interval against \(F_{\alpha,s,M}(T_n)\), against \(G_\alpha(\tau_n)\) where the moving family is legal, and against the resulting global benchmark \(C_{\mathrm{low}}r_n\).

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(s\in[1,2]\). All limits in the proof are as \(n\to\infty\). By the definitions of \(T_n\) and \(\tau_n\), and by \(\kappa_n>0\),
\[
 T_n\kappa_n^{1-1/s}
 =n\kappa_n^{2+1/s}\kappa_n^{1-1/s}
 =n\kappa_n^3
 =\tau_n.
 \tag{1}
\]

We first prove the subsequential partition. Every sequence in the extended half-line \([0,\infty]\) has a convergent subsequence: if its limit inferior is finite, choose successively an index at which the sequence is within \(1/j\) above its eventual infimum and use the eventual lower bound within \(1/j\); if its limit inferior is infinite, the sequence itself tends to infinity. Apply this fact first to \((\tau_n)\). After passage to a subsequence, exactly one of
\[
 \tau_n\to0,
 \qquad
 \tau_n\to\tau\in(0,\infty),
 \qquad
 \tau_n\to\infty
 \tag{2}
\]
holds. In the third case, apply the same fact to \((\lambda_n)\) along the selected subsequence. A further subsequence then has \(\lambda_n\to0\), \(\lambda_n\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\), or \(\lambda_n\to\infty\). These five alternatives are exactly the components specified in \(\text{def:recovery-regimes}\). Their defining limits are pairwise incompatible, so the selected subsequence lies in exactly one component of \(\mathfrak R\).

If \(s=1\), the definitions give
\[
 T_n=n\kappa_n^3=\tau_n,
 \qquad
 \lambda_n=\frac{T_n}{\log(e/\kappa_n)}
 =\frac{\tau_n}{\log(e/\kappa_n)}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Thus the finite positive slope face and the three divergent-\(\tau_n\) location-entropy faces are separated exactly as asserted in \(\text{def:recovery-regimes}\).

Now suppose \(s>1\) and set \(a_s=1-1/s>0\). By (1) and the definition of \(\lambda_n\),
\[
 \tau_n=\lambda_n\kappa_n^{a_s}\log(e/\kappa_n).
 \tag{4}
\]
Suppose first that \((\lambda_n)\) is eventually bounded. Then \(\kappa_n\to0\). Indeed, if not, some \(\varepsilon>0\) and a subsequence would satisfy \(\kappa_n\ge\varepsilon\); since also \(\kappa_n\le1/8\), on that subsequence
\[
 \lambda_n
 =\frac{n\kappa_n^{2+1/s}}{\log(e/\kappa_n)}
 \ge
 \frac{n\varepsilon^{2+1/s}}{\log(e/\varepsilon)}
 \longrightarrow\infty,
\]
contradicting eventual boundedness. Moreover,
\[
 x^{a_s}\log(e/x)\longrightarrow0
 \qquad (x\downarrow0).
 \tag{5}
\]
For completeness, put \(v=x^{-1}\). For \(v\ge1\),
\[
 \log v=\int_1^v z^{-1}\,dz
 \le\int_1^v z^{a_s/2-1}\,dz
 \le\frac{2}{a_s}v^{a_s/2},
\]
and hence \(x^{a_s}\log(e/x)\le v^{-a_s}+(2/a_s)v^{-a_s/2}\to0\). Equation (4), eventual boundedness of \(\lambda_n\), and (5) imply \(\tau_n\to0\).

Conversely, extend \(g_s(x)=x^{a_s}\log(e/x)\) to \(x=0\) by \(g_s(0)=0\). The preceding calculation proves continuity at zero; continuity away from zero and compactness therefore give
\[
 B_s:=\max_{0\le x\le1/8}g_s(x)<\infty.
\]
Because \(g_s(\kappa_n)>0\), (4) yields
\[
 \lambda_n=\frac{\tau_n}{g_s(\kappa_n)}
 \ge\frac{\tau_n}{B_s}.
\]
Thus \(\tau_n\to\infty\) implies \(\lambda_n\to\infty\).

We next certify the assertion that cutoff recovery alone need not yield shrinking minimax length. Fix \(s>1\). Since
\[
 \frac13<\frac{s}{2s+1},
\]
choose \(b\) strictly between these two numbers and define \(\kappa_n=8^{-1}n^{-b}\). This sequence is in \((0,1/8]\), and direct substitution gives
\[
 \tau_n=8^{-3}n^{1-3b}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{6}
\]
Writing \(p_s=2+1/s\), the choice \(b<s/(2s+1)=1/p_s\) gives \(1-bp_s>0\), and therefore
\[
 \lambda_n
 =\frac{8^{-p_s}n^{1-bp_s}}{\log(8e)+b\log n}
 \longrightarrow\infty.
 \tag{7}
\]
By \(\text{def:recovery-regimes}\), (7) is exactly \(\mathsf{CR}(s,\kappa_\bullet)\). By (6) and the definition of \(r_n\),
\[
 r_n
 =\min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}+\frac1{\tau_n}\right\}
 =1
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\). The global lower bound in \(\text{thm:integrated-and-bump-lower-frontier}\) consequently gives
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge C_{\mathrm{low}}r_n=C_{\mathrm{low}}>0
\]
eventually. Thus even information-theoretic cutoff recovery does not alone force the minimax expected length of honest connected intervals to vanish.

Finally, \(\text{thm:integrated-and-bump-lower-frontier}\) states, without a recovery restriction, that for every \(n\ge1\) and \(0<\kappa_n\le1/8\),
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge C_{\mathrm{low}}r_n.
\]
On the upper side, \(\text{def:profile-resolution-schedule}\) defines \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\) by requiring membership in \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{recovered}}\) together with three additional vanishing certificate conditions. Hence \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\subseteq\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{recovered}}\), and the conservative finite-grid attainment claim remains scoped only to \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\). No upper-bound or attainment assertion is proved here.
